```{r setup}
library(RDNowcast)
```
## The data

A data set is included in the `RDNowcast` package:

```{r data, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(RDNowcast)
library(lubridate)
library(flextable)

data <- RDNowcast::RDdata
data |> head(n = 10)
```

This data set, which consists of dates of death (reference_date) and reporting dates (report_date) can be used to generate nowcast estimates and, if the chosen date of analysis is sufficiently far in the past, to validate these estimates.

## Nowcasting the weekly number of deaths

### Preparing the data

We choose a date of analysis of 2026-04-30, which is a Thursday, one year in the past (i.e. before the most recent death date in the data set). We will nowcast 10 weekly counts, with the most recent count to be nowcasted for the week ending past Sunday (2025-08-10). 

Around the date 364 days before the date of analysis, five dates are chosen each into the past and ahead, separated by one week each and on the same day of the week as the date of analysis. The construction of this series of dates is supported by the function `RDNowcast::RDdates_create`.

These dates form the basis for the 11 overlapping 10-week periods, data from which will be used for training:

```{r data_prep, message = FALSE}
dateAnal <- as.Date("2026-07-09") # The date, the analysis is conducted

ncdates <- NCdates_create(data = data, NCdatesProp = seq.Date(dateAnal - 364 -5*7,dateAnal - 364 +5*7,by = "week"),
                            dateAnal = dateAnal)

recentRef <- "2026-07-05" # The most recent death date to be considered; does not have to be the end of a week

```

### Running the Nowcast

Once the date of analysis and the training time period have been chosen, the nowcast can be performed

```{r nowcast, message = FALSE}
# Pulling the complete data, not right-censored
fullData <- data |>  
  filter(reference_date<=recentRef) |> 
  mutate(week = floor_date(reference_date, unit = "week", week_start = 1)) |> 
  group_by(week) |> summarize(n = n()) |> ungroup() |> 
  tail(n = 10) |> 
  pull(n)

NCTable <-  RDNowcast(data = data, dateAnal = dateAnal, recentRef = recentRef, NCsize = 10,
                                          unit = "week",cnames = c("n","ll","ul","o"),tu_lab = "woche",NCdates = ncdates) |> 
  mutate(complete = fullData)

ft <- flextable(NCTable) |> 
  set_header_labels(values = c( "Week", "Median",  "Lower 95% Cred. Int.",  "Upper 95% Cred. Int.", "observed", "complete")) |> 
  flextable::align(align = "center", part = "body") |> flextable::colformat_num(big.mark=",", decimal.mark=".")
ft
```

## Nowcast based on Lawless (1994)

This method is widely used and mathematically elegant. The big advantage over our approach is that there is no need for a long time series of data.  

```{r lawless_nowcast, message = FALSE}
# Pulling the complete data, not right-censored

fullData2 <- data |>  
  filter(reference_date<=recentRef) |> 
  mutate(week = floor_date(reference_date, unit = "week", week_start = 1)) |> 
  group_by(week) |> summarize(n = n()) |> ungroup() |> 
  tail(n = 12) |> 
  pull(n)

NCTable2 <-  LawlessNowcast(data = data, dateAnal = dateAnal, maxdelay = 10,
                                          cnames = c("n","ll","ul","o"),tu_lab = "woche") |> mutate(complete = fullData2)

ft2 <- flextable(NCTable2) |> 
  set_header_labels(values = c( "Week", "Median",  "Lower 95% Cred. Int.",  "Upper 95% Cred. Int.", "observed", "complete")) |> 
  flextable::align(align = "center", part = "body") |> flextable::colformat_num(big.mark=",", decimal.mark=".")
ft2
```
